## 1. Learning objectives
- use `if / else if / else` to classify stock as OUT / LOW / OK;
- use arrays and a `for` loop to process every product;
- build report text with `StringBuilder` and `String.format`;
- finish **Milestone M1** and run it end to end.

## 2. Plain-English explanation
- An **`if`** statement asks a yes/no question. The first branch whose answer is *yes* runs; the rest are skipped.
  Order matters: check `OUT` before `LOW`, because 0 is also "at or below" the reorder level.
- An **array** is a numbered row of boxes of the same type. Counting starts at **0**:
  `quantities[0]` is the first one. `quantities.length` is how many there are.
- A **`for` loop** repeats a block. `for (int i = 0; i < names.length; i++)` means
  "start `i` at 0, keep going while `i` is less than the length, add 1 each time".
- **Parallel arrays** (`names[i]`, `quantities[i]` describe the same product) are a beginner's table. In
  week 3 you replace them with a `Product` class — and you will see why that is nicer.
- **`reorder level`**: when stock falls to this number you should buy more.

## 3. Runnable sample code
`examples/Decisions.java` — run: `java lessons/03-decisions-and-loops/examples/Decisions.java`
```java
for (int i = 0; i < quantities.length; i++) {
    if (quantities[i] <= 0)               status = "OUT";
    else if (quantities[i] <= reorderLevel) status = "LOW";
    else                                   status = "OK";
}
```

## 7. Common mistakes and troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` | Loop runs `i <= length` or arrays have different sizes | Use `i < names.length`; keep arrays the same length |
| Sugar shows `LOW` instead of `OUT` | `LOW` checked before `OUT` | Test `quantity <= 0` first |
| Report has an empty last line | Added `"\n"` after every row | Add it *before* each row (or only between rows) |
| Columns not aligned | Wrong format widths | Copy the `%-14s%5d  %s` patterns exactly |
| `=` vs `==` confusion | `=` assigns, `==` compares | In `if`, use `<=`, `==`, etc. |
| Infinite loop | Forgot `i++` | Ctrl+C, then fix the loop header |
